title: BRICKSTORM Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate and identify malicious activity related to the BRICKSTORM Backdoor on the target host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target host has been exhibiting unusual network activity. Your task is to investigate and identify any malicious activity related to the BRICKSTORM Backdoor. This backdoor is known to use techniques such as systemd service manipulation and process hiding to evade detection. This scenario will guide you through the investigation phase of a realistic compromise lifecycle, including initial compromise, lateral movement, and data exfiltration phases. The learning objective is to develop your skills in using systemctl, process and service investigation techniques, persistence mechanism identification, and malicious artifact location.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target host's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target host. Enumerate running services and distinguish legitimate from suspicious services. The flag is the name of the suspicious service (e.g., vnetd.service).

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services can be listed to identify running services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command to list all running services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The command to list running services is `systemctl list-units --type=service`.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Identify persistence mechanisms such as systemd, cron, scheduled tasks, or registry entries. The flag is the name of the persistence mechanism (e.g., vnetd.service).

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms can be identified by examining systemd service files and timers.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command to list all systemd service files.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The command to list systemd service files is `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service`.

levels.title: Locate Malicious Artifact
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity. Correlate processes with files on disk and identify malicious artifacts. The flag is the path to the malicious artifact (e.g., /usr/local/bin/lab-checkin.sh).

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Processes can be correlated with files on disk to identify malicious artifacts.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command to list processes and their associated files.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The command to list processes and their associated files is `ps aux | grep vnetd`.
